name: model_unavailable
inspect: classify and draft events with status unavailable in the window: attempts and last_error
the provider's status page and the retry backoff in the step durations
/health for the running mode, client, and versions
respond: If the rate stays above threshold for a second window, switch the deployment to rules mode (ASSISTANT_MODE=rules) per the runbook; requests are still answered from templates and a person still sends. Switch back when two consecutive windows on the model are clean.
why: An unavailable model step is the failure the retry policy could not fix. One window is enough to act because every affected request costs an agent the draft.

name: retries_rising
inspect: failed_calls and last_error on classify and draft events: timeouts or rate limits
latency p95 in the same windows: retries add backoff before anything is unavailable
respond: Nothing is broken yet: requests complete on a retry. Lower ASSISTANT_CONCURRENCY to ease rate limits, confirm the rules-mode fallback is ready (runbook), and watch the next window. If the unavailable rule fires next, switch without waiting for its second window.
why: Retries that succeed are the hour before an outage. Seeing them early turns the outage response from a second-window decision into a first-window one.

name: latency_p95
inspect: per-step p50 durations: is it classify, draft, or both
output token counts on draft events: longer drafts or a slower provider
attempts on step events: retries add backoff to the total
respond: Confirm it is the provider and not a batch with unusual concurrency. If the provider, lower ASSISTANT_CONCURRENCY and raise ASSISTANT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS within the objective; if p95 stays above 8 s for two more windows, rules mode.
why: One slow window is noise; two consecutive two-hour windows over the objective is a change agents will feel. At the assistant's volume (about seven requests an hour) a one-hour window rarely holds enough requests to judge a percentile.

name: escalation_share
inspect: the reasons mix in the window: unknown_category, no_reference_article, hostile, legal, or model steps unavailable
the category mix against the baseline week (drift report)
whether a prompt variant or version changed in the window (versions on request events)
respond: Open a drift investigation. Do not roll anything back on this alert alone: a change in what customers ask is not a fault in the assistant, and the fix may be a knowledge article.
why: Escalation share moves with the traffic mix as much as with the assistant, so it is judged over half-day windows and needs two in a row before anyone is told, and its response is an investigation, not a switch.

name: flagged_drafts
inspect: checks events: which problems fire (unverifiable_promise, ungrounded_number, ungrounded_link)
the prompt version on request events: did it change
the model name: did the provider move the alias
respond: Pin the prompt and model versions that were running before the change; if the model alias moved, set ASSISTANT_MODEL to the previous version. Run the development split of the evaluation suite on the replay client to confirm the drafts changed.
why: The checks catch promises and invented numbers deterministically; a rising rate is the earliest sign that the drafts changed shape.

name: spend
inspect: input and output tokens per step over the day: longer prompts, longer drafts, or more retries
the prompt variant running: v2 sends the article list on every classification
respond: No automatic action. Confirm the rates, then decide with the owner whether the spend is the new normal or a regression to fix.
why: Cost needs a day to mean anything and is measured against the charter's gate, at rates the operator supplies.
